newsitem.title: GERMANY: Megret says NF to "scare" immigrants in France.
newsitem.headline: Megret says NF to "scare" immigrants in France.

text.p: Catherine Megret, the new far-right mayor of the French city of Vitrolles, said in an interview on Monday that France was in a state of emergency and her National Front wanted to instil fear in immigrants.

A political newcomer who ran in place of her husband, NF number two Bruno Megret, the new mayor told the Berliner Zeitung she would cut almost all social payments to immigrants and fire social workers to hire more police for a crime crackdown.
Pro-immigrant groups would lose their subsidies and most left-wing books would be removed from municipal libraries, she said. Rap and black musicians would also be unwelcome.
"Our voters wanted us to scare people who don't belong," Megret said in her first interview since taking control of the town hall in the southern French city on February 16.
"You must see that we here in France are now in a state of emergency," she said. "We have to act fast."
Vitrolles was the fourth southern city taken over by the National Front after Toulon, Marignane and Orange.

The Berliner Zeitung described the interview as "painful" but said it printed it to show that "French racism uses arguments that have become acceptable elsewhere... Megret's comments may be only the start of a menacing development."
Megret told the newspaper: "We will immediately stop all state aid to immigrants and give the money to French people. Our motto is: French first.
"Unfortunately, there are some services we will have to continue providing, but there won't be one centime more for them beyond that.

"You'll see how quickly they disappear from here. They're only here for the money. If we could do it at communal level, we would also take a look at the naturalisation files for some foreigners that are now running around with a French passport."

"We will bring order into culture," she went on. "This whole rap scene, for example, is not our thing and there will be no more aid for it. French cultural and Provencal culture will take priority here... I find modern culture is not worth much."

Megret accused the left wing of banning NF publications from public libraries for years and asked: "Why not try it the other way around? But we won't go as far as to ban the leftist press. That would be another argument for the left."
The new mayor accused social workers hired by the city's previous socialist administration of making common cause with young criminals instead of helping to prevent crime.

"We will abolish these posts completely and hire policemen in their place who, instead of trying to prevent crime, will crack down hard," she said. "We have to pursue and punish criminals... it's mostly the immigrants."
Megret, whose grandparents were Jewish immigrants from Russia, saw no contradiction between her family background and her present views against immigration.
"That was the past; the situation today is completely different," she said. Present-day immigrants "certainly have not suffered as much as my family did back then in Russia."
The new mayor said she planned to focus mostly on social problems in Vitrolles while her husband Bruno made the important political decisions.
"My husband is the locomotive and we are all just the railway cars," she said. "My husband's voters knew who was standing behind me. They voted for Megret and got Megret."
She also praised NF leader Jean-Marie Le Pen for what she called his clear explanations of racial differences.

"Every halfway reasonable person would agree there are differences between the races," she said. "There are simply genetic differences. Jean-Marie Le Pen explained it well when he said the blacks were more talented for sports and dancing than whites and that whites had other strengths."
